# Enter in a grid picker editor opens the picker of the edit it ends

## Context

Leaf of #18762 (grid cell editing, responsibility 2: the interaction contract). Found while evaluating the epic on the public example `examples/grid/cellEditing`, left unowned in the leaf map, measured today.

In a grid, Enter in an editor commits: keys route through `grid.View`, "the grid's single key registry" (`src/grid/plugin/CellEditing.mjs`, class docblock). A picker field has its own Enter: `form.field.Picker#onKeyDownEnter` opens the picker. Both run on the same key — the field's first, because the key event reaches the deepest component first.

## The Problem

Measured under Playwright (Chromium) on the example's Date column, with a worker-side probe on `Picker#createPicker` / `#showPicker` and a main-thread `MutationObserver` on `.neo-picker-container`, 3 of 3 runs each:

| Case | App Worker | DOM |
|---|---|---|
| fresh Date editor, Enter | `showPicker` → `createPicker`: a whole picker, date selector included, is built for the editor the same key destroys | no picker node |
| Date editor after a picker visit (picker instance exists), Enter | `showPicker` | the picker node is inserted and removed in the same millisecond, ~20 ms after the key |

So every Enter-commit on a Date or Time editor builds or mounts a picker for an editor that is already ending. The mount for a dying owner is also the source of a flake: on a loaded CI runner the picker node has been seen to stay in `document.body` after the editor was gone (#18880 removed the assertion that tripped on it, and recorded the orphan as a defect-note).

`form.field.ComboBox` and its subclasses (`Color`, `Country`, `Chip`) are not affected: `keys` is a plain config, so their map (`Down`, `Escape`) replaces the base map and has no Enter.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/form/field/Picker.mjs`: `keys: {Enter: 'onKeyDownEnter', Escape: 'onKeyDownEscape'}`; `onKeyDownEnter()` → `!pickerIsMounted && showPicker()`. `Date.mjs` and `Time.mjs` override it and call `super` for the closed case.
- `onKeyDownEscape()` already shows the shape of a key the field owns: it acts only while the picker is mounted, then sets `data.cancelBubble` and returns `false`, so the grid's Escape never sees it — the two-step Escape `CellEditingExample.spec.mjs` pins.
- Enter has no such split: the field acts, claims nothing, and `grid.View`'s registry runs `grid.plugin.CellEditing#onEnterKey` → `completeEdit()` → `editor.destroy()` → `Picker#destroy` unmounts and destroys the picker it was just asked to show.
- `Picker` already has the sibling switch for the other implicit open: `showPickerOnFocus` (default `false`).
- The plugin creates editors in `startEdit()` as `{module: TextField, ...column.editor, …}` and already treats editor capabilities as optional (`editor.selectText?.()`).

## The Fix

- `form.field.Picker`: a config `showPickerOnEnter` (default `true`, today's behaviour everywhere outside a grid), read by `onKeyDownEnter`.
- `grid.plugin.CellEditing#startEdit`: a picker editor is created with `showPickerOnEnter: false`, unless its column's `editor` config says otherwise. In a grid, Enter is the grid's.
- Witnesses: a unit arm on `Picker` (the config off → Enter creates and shows no picker), and the e2e `date:` arm in `CellEditingExample.spec.mjs` gets back the assertion #18880 had to drop, on the right premise this time: no picker node is ever sighted after the committing Enter (`MutationObserver`, ordering proven by the editor's removal).

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `form.field.Picker#showPickerOnEnter` (new config) | `src/form/field/Picker.mjs` (`showPickerOnFocus` is the precedent) | `true`: Enter opens a closed picker, as today. `false`: Enter is left to the field's host | default `true` — no behaviour change outside grids | config docblock | unit arm |
| `grid.plugin.CellEditing#startEdit` (editor defaults) | `src/grid/plugin/CellEditing.mjs` | picker editors get `showPickerOnEnter: false`; `column.editor` can override | — | method docblock | e2e arm on the public example |

## Decision Record impact

none

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: with `showPickerOnEnter: false`, Enter on a closed picker field neither creates nor shows a picker; the default keeps today's behaviour. Unit tier.
- [ ] AC-2: Enter in a grid Date editor commits with no picker node sighted at any point after the key, fresh and after a picker visit; the arm is red on `dev` for the after-a-visit case. e2e tier, public example.
- [ ] AC-3: the existing `date:` arms (trigger opens the picker inside the session, two-step Escape) stay green.

## Out of Scope

- **A keyboard path to open a picker inside a grid editor.** Measured today: in a Date editor ArrowDown and Alt+ArrowDown open nothing, and Enter — the field's only open key — is the grid's commit, so a keyboard user cannot reach the date picker in a grid at all (the value itself stays typeable: the input is `type="date"`). This ticket does not change that; it only stops building pickers nobody sees. Facts for whoever takes it: `util.KeyNavigation` key maps carry no modifiers; on `type="date"` the plain arrow keys step the focused segment natively; the WAI-ARIA date-picker combobox pattern opens on Alt+ArrowDown; `ComboBox` already opens on `Down`.
- What Enter means while the picker is open and focus is in the input (today: the grid commits, measured).
- `Picker#onKeyDownEnter(data, callback, callbackScope)` forwards two arguments `showPicker()` does not take — dead parameters through `Date.mjs` / `Time.mjs`.
- The engine-level race behind the orphan node (a floating component destroyed while its mount is in flight). This ticket removes one producer of that race, not the race.

## Avoided Traps

- **Claiming Enter in the field (`cancelBubble`), as Escape does.** Then a closed Date editor could never be committed by Enter: every Enter would open the picker again.
- **Teaching the field about grids** (reading the `neo-grid-editor` class in `Picker`). The host knows its key contract; the field should not know its hosts.
